operations.description: DRS processes synchronized objects and allows you to add rules for selected objects.
This API is used to perform batch pre-check to check whether the migration can be performed.
This API is used to query the pre-check results of tasks in batches.
This API is used to create real-time migration, real-time synchronization, and real-time DR tasks in batches based on different request parameters.
This API is used to asynchronously create real-time migration, synchronization, or DR tasks in batches based on different request parameters.
This API is used to add resource tags in batches.
This API is used to stop tasks in batches or delete real-time migration, real-time synchronization, and real-time DR tasks.
This API is used to delete tasks with specified IDs in batches.
This API is used to batch delete tags from a specified instance.
This API is used to batch perform operations on tasks with specified IDs.
This API is used to query task details in batches by task ID.
This API is used to query task statuses in batches by task ID.
This API is used to query the full progress and incremental delay information in batches based on the task ID.
This API is used to query Recovery Point Objective (RPO) and Recovery Time Objective (RTO).
This API is used to query details about DR initialization objects in batches by task ID.
This API is used to query the DR initialization progress in batches based on the task ID. Virtual IDs cannot be queried.
This API is used to change the passwords of the source and destination databases after a task is started.
This API is used to retry failed migration tasks.

The API is used to set whether to migrate all Definers to the user in batches.- If you select **Yes**, the Definers of all source database objects will be migrated to the user. Other users do not have permissions on database objects unless they are authorized.- If you select **No**, the Definers of all source database objects will not be changed. You need to migrate all accounts and permissions of the source database in the next step.
This API is used to select the databases or tables to be migrated.

- This API is used to configure synchronization policies in batches, including conflict policies, DROP DATASE filtering, and object synchronization scope. - This API is used to set the Kafka synchronization policy.
This API is used to set exception notifications in batches. This parameter cannot be set for stopped tasks. - You can select an existing SMN topic or manually enter a mobile number or email address.

This API is used to enable or disable flow control for tasks. By default, the migration speed is not limited after a task is created.- **Control**: You can customize the maximum migration speed.- **No control**: The migration speed is not limited and the outbound bandwidth of the source database is maximally used, which drives up read consumption on the source database accordingly. For example, if the outbound bandwidth of the source database is 100 MB/s and 80% bandwidth is used, the I/O consumption on the source database is 80 MB/s.

To ensure that service applications are not affected after the migration, DRS provides parameter comparison to help you compare parameters between the source and destination databases. This API is used to obtain database parameters of the source and destination databases.
This API is used to start real-time migration, synchronization, and disaster recovery tasks in batches.
This API is used to pause tasks in batches.
This API is used to batch stop tasks with a specified ID.
This API is used to perform a batch primary/standby switchover.
This API is used to add or delete tags in batches.
This API is used to modify task names or descriptions in batches and set exception notification.
This API is used to set the users and roles to be migrated in batches.
- This API is used to test connections in cluster mode. - This API is used to test connections for a primary/standby task.
This API is used to test connections in batches.
This API is used to change the billing mode of a real-time synchronization or DR task from pay-per-use to yearly/monthly.
This API is used to verify data filtering rules.
This API is used to clear DDL alarms.
This API is used to collect the column information about a specified database table.

This API is used to submit the query of database object information. Example: - If **type** is set to **source**, table information in the source database is queried. - If table information in the source database changes, set **type** to **source** and **is_refresh** to **true**. - If the volume of the database table data that has been synchronized to the destination database is too large and data needs to be loaded to the cache, set **type** to **synchronized**.

This API is used to submit the query of database object information. Example: - If **type** is set to **source**, table information in the source database is queried. - If table information in the source database changes, set **type** to **source** and **is_refresh** to **true**. - If the volume of the database table data that has been synchronized to the destination database is too large and data needs to be loaded to the cache, set **type** to **synchronized**.
This API is used to collect database position information.

This API is used to submit the tasks created asynchronously in batches. After tasks are asynchronously created in batches or parameters are updated, the system automatically verifies the parameters. After the parameters of all tasks are verified and no error is reported, you can call this API to create DRS instances.
This API allows you to clone the configuration of existing synchronization tasks.
This API is used to query the number of resource instances.
This API is used to export the comparison result file.
This API is used to create a comparison task

This API is used to create a single connection. The connection database can be an on-premises database or an RDS DB instance. Currently, the supported DB engines include MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, and MongoDB.
This API is used to create a data-level table comparison task.
This API is used to create a single task. You can create a real-time migration, synchronization, or DR task based on different request parameters.
This API is used to create an object-level comparison task.

This API is used to configure backup migration tasks in three common scenarios. Backup migration supports the following common scenarios: - Full migration of backup files in OBS buckets - Full+incremental migration of backup files in OBS buckets - Full migration of the RDS full backup

This API is used to query the migration progress of different migration tasks. Notes: - Currently, you can view migration details only for real-time migration tasks from MySQL to MySQL, from MySQL to GaussDB(for MySQL), from MongoDB to DDS, and from DDS to MongoDB and all real-time synchronization tasks. - Before the task is completed, do not modify the information about all source and destination database users, passwords, and permissions. - If the status indicates a full or incremental migration is complete, there may still be triggers or events to be migrated before the entire task is finished.
